title: Linux_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_e1a
description: Investigate and identify malicious activity in a network experiencing unusual traffic patterns and potential unauthorized access.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential unauthorized access. Your task is to investigate and identify any malicious activity, determine its scope, and recommend containment measures.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

To proceed, enter 'start' in the access field.
levels.local_content:
You have local access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

To proceed, enter 'start' in the access field.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that communicates with an external host?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is the beacon service running on the system.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by understanding the system's normal behavior and look for deviations.

hints.title: Actionable Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services and look for unusual ones.

hints.title: Detailed Hint
hints.content: Check the network connections of each service using `ss -tulnp` and look for connections to external hosts.

levels.title: Identify Excessive Network Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating excessive network traffic?
levels.solution: Examine systemd timers and services for unusual activity. The service generating excessive network traffic is the flood service running on the system.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Look for services that are generating more traffic than usual or expected.

hints.title: Actionable Hint
hints.content: Use the command `nethogs` to monitor network traffic per process and identify the service consuming the most bandwidth.

hints.title: Detailed Hint
hints.content: Check the service details using `systemctl status <service_name>` and look for any unusual configurations or timers.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Investigate systemd timers and services for clues about automatic execution. The persistence mechanism is the systemd timer or service responsible for starting the suspicious service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms often involve systemd timers or services that start automatically.

hints.title: Actionable Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers and look for any associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Detailed Hint
hints.content: Check the timer details using `systemctl status <timer_name>` and look for any unusual configurations.
